risks.description: Prose governance can drift or be weakened without an obvious runtime failure.
risks.mitigation: The machine-readable profile and dependency-free verifier validate required sections, semantic clauses, exact authority order, ownership, stop conditions, human authority, confidentiality, and conflicting statements.

risks.description: Platform Contracts governance could be misread as authority to implement P0-T02B, P0-T02C, P0-T02D, or P0-T03.
risks.mitigation: AGENTS.md, the profile, verifier, tests, and scope evidence explicitly keep all four successor tasks not-started.

risks.description: The local Node.js runtime is 25.9.0 rather than the frozen application baseline 24.18.0.
risks.mitigation: The new verifier uses only stable Node.js built-ins and no external packages; validation should be repeated under the pinned runtime when it becomes available.

risks.description: A passing governance verifier could be mistaken for merge, architecture, production, package, or manufacturing approval.
risks.mitigation: Every governance representation remains checkpoint-review-required and explicitly reserves those decisions for humans.

risks.description: Manufacturing OS has pre-existing uncommitted and untracked data outside this task's worktree.
risks.mitigation: The consumer was inspected read-only, not modified, and cross-repository validation used only pinned committed Git objects and temporary detached clones.
